historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: 2028 Capital Markets Day targets haircut; no historical CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+11.0%) diverges >30% from revenue (-1.9%) and EPS (n/m: FY2020 was a loss). The equity CAGR is an artefact of the FY2020 deferred-tax-asset write-down and its FY2022 re-recognition, not of retained growth; revenue has shrunk from 23.6bn (FY2016) to 19.9bn. None of the trailing CAGRs is a credible forward rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (OCF - capex - lease principal - SBC - interest received), endpoint-sensitive: FY2022 (442) and FY2020 (937) are the bases. Reported FCF (OCF - capex) 5yr CAGR is +2.7% against -4.5% on the owner basis: SBC rose from 76 to 337 and interest received from 33 to 163 over the period, so a growing share of reported FCF is stock-paid or earned by the cash pile. EPS 3yr CAGR is measured from the FY2022 peak (0.75) that included a ~2.5bn deferred-tax benefit.

scenario_narratives.base: Network Infrastructure (optical, IP, fixed) grows 6-8% on hyperscaler and AI data-centre demand with Infinera fully integrated, while Mobile Infrastructure (RAN, core, patent licensing) is flat: group revenue grows 4-5% to ~22.8bn by 2028, then fades to 2.5%. Comparable operating profit reaches ~2.7bn in 2028 - the bottom of the 2.7-3.2bn Capital Markets Day range, a haircut for Nokia's record of restructurings that delivered late - and the cash EBITDA margin tops out at 16.5% (about 13% comparable). Restructuring cash never fully disappears, patent licensing renews at similar rates, and EUR/USD is neutral.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-networking pivot works at scale: optical and IP switching into AI data centres (Infinera, SR Linux on Nvidia Spectrum-X) compound at double digits, AI-RAN and early 6G restart RAN growth late in the decade, and trusted-vendor and defence demand adds on top. Revenue grows 7-9% through 2030, comparable operating profit clears the top of the 2028 range (~3.4bn) on mix and operating leverage, and the cash EBITDA margin reaches 19%. The exit multiple is 18x rather than 15x because a larger share of the business is growing infrastructure and licence annuity instead of shrinking RAN.
scenario_narratives.bear: The last decade repeats: revenue fell from 23.6bn to 19.9bn over FY2016-25 and does not grow. The 5G RAN cycle keeps maturing with Huawei and ZTE pricing pressure outside protected markets, hyperscaler AI capex pauses so optical growth only offsets RAN decline, a weaker USD and tariffs keep clipping margins, and the two-segment reorganisation costs another round of restructuring cash. Comparable operating profit stays near 2.0bn, the 2028 target is missed, a major licence renewal lands at a lower rate, and the cash EBITDA margin stays at 13-13.5%. No solvency issue - 3.4bn net cash - so this is a stagnation case, not a distress case.

valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note: Model approach: the multiples sanity check tripped on one rule of three - the base-case value implies 92.5x SBC-adjusted trailing P/E against a 10-year average of 37.8x - and after review the drivers were left unchanged. The trip is a denominator artefact, not a sign the DCF is paying a multiple the market never has. FY2025 reported net income was EUR 651m (EUR 314m after SBC) against roughly EUR 2.0bn of comparable operating profit: reported operating income of EUR 885m sits about EUR 1.1bn below the comparable figure (restructuring, acquired-intangible amortisation after Infinera and similar items - inferred from the gap, no filing text was available to itemise it), on top of the ~EUR 230m currency and EUR 50-80m tariff hits to comparable profit itself. On comparable profit taxed at 25% the base value is about 19x earnings (about 24x if SBC is deducted again, 17-21x excluding net cash), in line with the two undistorted years in the history (FY2021 21.0x, FY2024 20.8x). The 37.8x average is itself built from only five usable years, of which one is a deferred-tax windfall (FY2022, 5.7x) and two are depressed-earnings years (FY2023 37x, FY2025 104x); the market's own FY2025 year-end multiple on the same basis was 104x, above the implied one. The rules that do not depend on trailing net income pass: implied P/B 1.39x against a 1.40x average, implied P/Sales 1.46x against a 1.12x average and 1.65x maximum. The four documented fixes were each tested and rejected: (1) not peak earnings - FY2025 owner FCF of 744 is below the six-year median of ~840 and year-1 modelled FCF is flat on FY2025 before working capital; (2) no WACC premium - Nokia is a large, liquid, net-cash company whose operating profit range is under 3x peak-to-trough, so none of the premium criteria is met, and cyclicality is carried by the 25% bear weight; (3) growth - the base path (4-5% fading to 2.5%) is above the negative ten-year revenue CAGR and is the assumption most open to challenge, but it rests on the 2028 targets at their low end and the stagnation record is the bear case at 25%; capping the base at the historical CAGR would turn the base into the bear; (4) no historical EV/EBITDA exists to set an exit cap (no EBITDA or D&A history in the metrics), and the terminal capitalisation multiples of 12x/15x/18x already bound the terminal value. Framing: the weighted value sits below the market price, so this is not a cheap-turnaround call - it is a mid-teens-multiple networks business whose value depends on converting the 2028 plan into owner cash.
valuation_philosophy.summary: Nokia is valued on the cash its networks and patent businesses produce after SBC, lease payments, recurring restructuring cash and interest earned on its cash pile, not on comparable operating profit or volatile reported net income. Mid-cycle owner FCF has been EUR 0.7-0.9bn on ~EUR 20bn of revenue; the valuation question is how much of the 2028 plan (comparable operating profit up ~40-60%) converts into owner cash, and whether the AI-networking growth is durable or one hyperscaler capex cycle.
key_risks_to_valuation: The P/E sanity rule trips (92.5x implied vs 37.8x average) because trailing reported net income is depressed; the valuation was deliberately not cut to clear it - see sanity_check_note. If FY2026 reported earnings do not recover toward comparable profit, the gap is structural (permanent restructuring) and the base margin path is too high
Anchors are stale: balance sheet, share count and guidance are as of 2025-12-31 because no 2026 interim data was available; 2026 results could move net cash and the year-1 drivers materially
Terminal value is 45-63% of enterprise value across the scenarios (56% base) and in the base case rests on a 16.5% cash EBITDA margin Nokia has not sustained in the last decade

EBITDA margin is defined on a cash basis after restructuring; if restructuring cash genuinely ends after 2028 the base case is ~1pp of margin too low, if it rises with the reorganisation it is too high
EUR/USD: a large share of revenue is USD-linked while the model is in EUR, and the per-share values are converted to USD at a single spot rate
Patent-licensing renewals (Apple, Samsung and others) are lumpy, high-margin and outside the equipment cycle; one adverse renewal moves owner FCF by a double-digit percentage
The pension surplus (EUR 4.4bn net) and venture/associate investments (~EUR 0.9bn) are excluded; counting them would add up to ~EUR 0.9/share, an unfunded-plan view would subtract ~EUR 0.3/share

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 5.86-17.45. FX from Yahoo EURUSD=X; parity checked against NOKIA.HE.
data_sources.financials: research/NOK/Reports/NOK_Metrics.csv (FY2014-FY2025, SEC XBRL ifrs-full) plus component lines read directly from the SEC companyfacts API for CIK 924613 (FY2025 20-F): interest received, lease payments, income taxes paid, D&A, share repurchases, interest-bearing investments, borrowings, NCI, dilutive shares, pensions. No quarterly data and no filing text.
data_sources.qualitative: research/NOK/Reports/NOK_Analysis.json (segments, Infinera, Nvidia partnership, 2028 targets, 2025 FX/tariff headwinds).

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 5,582.5m shares outstanding at 2025-12-31 (5,742m issued less ~160m treasury, FY2025 20-F XBRL NumberOfSharesOutstanding) plus 87m dilutive share-award effect (DilutiveEffectOfShareOptionsOnNumberOfOrdinaryShares). Includes the ~166m shares issued to Nvidia in 2025 (EUR 859m proceeds). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.cash_composition: Cash and equivalents 5,462 + current interest-bearing financial investments 961 + non-current interest-bearing financial investments 368 = 6,791; borrowings 3,413 (current 1,084 + long-term 2,329). Net cash 3,378 follows Nokia's own net-cash definition (the same construction reproduces Nokia's reported 4,323 for FY2023 and 4,854 for FY2024). Lease liabilities (1,000) are EXCLUDED because the lease payment is charged in the flows.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2025 operating cash flow 2,071 - capex 606 - lease principal 221 (IFRS 16, in financing). Nokia's own headline free cash flow (OCF - capex) is 1,465.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F XBRL AdjustmentsForSharebasedPayments (cash-flow add-back). No combined SBC-plus-withholding-tax figure is tagged and no filing text was available to check for net-share-settlement taxes, so the charge may be slightly understated.
inputs.fx_note: EUR->USD 1.1028, Yahoo EURUSD=X at 2026-11-13T22:29Z. ADR ratio 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share, confirmed by parity: NOKIA.HE EUR 7.294 (2026-11-13 Helsinki close) x 1.1028 = USD 8.04 against the NYSE close in current_price, a 0.3% tie. Unsuffixed per-share values are USD (quote currency); EUR twins are the model currency. refresh_price does not move fx_rate - refresh it with the price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built: ~2.7% Bund risk-free + ~5.5% ERP x beta ~1.1 gives cost of equity ~8.75%; the company is net cash, so WACC ~8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios - cyclicality, RAN decline and AI-capex dependency are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full lease cash payment (principal 221 + interest 35 = 256, 1.29% of revenue) charged via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (~1,119 total less ~220 ROU = ~900, 4.5% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI (EUR 91m book, profit share 9m) deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: network equipment + patent licensing) with the non-US adaptations - EUR flows bridged to a USD ADR quote, lease treatment B, NCI in the bridge, EUR-built WACC. STALE ANCHORS: the latest balance sheet and share count available are 2025-12-31 (FY2025 20-F XBRL); Nokia's 2026 6-K interim reports carry no XBRL and no filing text was available, so net cash, share count, buyback pace and FY2026 guidance are NOT refreshed for 2026 - replace them when 2026 interim data is loaded. MID-CYCLE: net income is too volatile to anchor on (FY2020 loss on a DTA write-down, FY2022 4.25bn on DTA re-recognition, 0.65-1.3bn since), so the forward build is anchored on cash earnings instead: FY2025 pre-tax, pre-working-capital operating cash earnings were 2,725 (13.7% of revenue, after restructuring cash, before SBC and leases), and owner FCF averaged 704 over FY2023-25 and 863 over FY2020-25 against 744 in FY2025 - FY2025 is close to mid-cycle, not a peak or trough. EBITDA margin in the paths is on that cash basis (pre-SBC, pre-lease, AFTER recurring restructuring cash), which is roughly comparable operating margin + 3.5pp. PENSIONS: net defined-benefit surplus of 4,433 (assets 6,380, liabilities 1,947) is neither added nor deducted - the surplus sits mainly in US plans and is not freely accessible; treating the net as zero is conservative. Venture-fund and equity-method investments (~0.9bn book) are also left out of the bridge. BUYBACKS: 624 of repurchases in FY2025 (680 in FY2024) fund the flat count against 337 of SBC. Interest paid (212) is left inside last_fcf, so the FY0 base is slightly conservative versus a strictly unlevered figure; the forward build is unlevered. The 52-week range is wide (5.86-17.45) and the current quote is near the low end; no cause could be verified from the files on hand.

base.margin_note: FY2028 model EBIT margin 9.3% on ~22.8bn revenue corresponds to ~12% comparable operating margin, i.e. ~2.7bn - the bottom of the 2.7-3.2bn target.
base.tax_note: FY2025 cash tax 396 was ~32% of model EBIT; fades to 25% (Nokia's long-run comparable rate) as Finnish deferred tax assets (3.6bn net) are used. Not taken below 25%: most cash tax is paid outside Finland.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (above the 15% default): flat-to-shrinking revenue with repeated restructuring is Nokia's actual ten-year record, and FX/tariffs forced a guidance cut as recently as 2025. Base 50%: the low end of management's 2028 target, which trailing results and the Infinera integration support. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs sustained hyperscaler AI capex, Nokia winning share in data-centre switching against Cisco/Arista/Ciena, and a RAN recovery to all go right together, and the AI-networking revenue is still unproven at scale.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: cyclicality

sanity_check.fix_applied: none - accepted with documented rationale (one fix pass, drivers unchanged). The single trip (implied P/E 92.5x vs 37.8x average) is a denominator artefact: FY2025 SBC-adjusted net income of ~EUR 314m against ~EUR 2.0bn comparable operating profit; on comparable earnings the base value is ~19-24x, in line with the undistorted history years (FY2021 21.0x, FY2024 20.8x). P/B (1.39x vs 1.40x avg) and P/Sales (1.46x vs 1.65x max) pass. Peak-earnings, WACC-premium and growth-cap fixes tested and rejected; exit-multiple cap not computable (no historical EV/EBITDA). Full reasoning in valuation_philosophy.sanity_check_note.
